sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry (L6/L7): surface APC signal and total GFP signal both detected, confirming surface trafficking of HA-tagged GluA2 flip and flop variants. AP-tag KI (L4): endogenous GluA2-containing AMPARs successfully biotinylated and labelled with avidin probes at the cell surface, with TEV-reversible labelling. SEP KI (L3): surface-localised fluorescence confirmed. No electrophysiological function assay reported for the HA-tagged constructs in these studies.
sites.rationale: L6 uniquely pins the junction: the HA tag sits 'between the signal peptide and the amino-terminal domain', which in UniProt canonical numbering places the insert after residue 24 (the last SP residue, S) and before residue 25 (N, the first mature residue). Python confirms seq[23]='S' and seq[24]='N'. The site is 521 residues from TM1 (546), well clear of any TM boundary. Six independent ledger lines (L1–L4, L6–L7, L9) all report tolerated N-terminal tags on full-length, membrane-anchored GluA2, and none names any other extracellular position, making this the sole ledger-supported surface site. Validation is classified surface_only because the flow-cytometry and surface-labelling assays confirm trafficking but no electrophysiological function measurement was reported for the tagged constructs. L6 (PMC12152890): full-length GluA2 (flip and flop) with an HA tag placed explicitly 'between the signal peptide and the amino-terminal domain', expressed in HEK cells; L7 (same paper) confirms surface display by flow cytometry (APC surface signal vs GFP total signal). Corroborated by: L1/L2 (PMC11798926) HA-GluA2 live surface-labelled in COS7 cells; L4 (PMC9328687) AP-tag CRISPR knock-in at endogenous GluA2 N-terminus enabling BirA biotinylation surface labelling; L3 (PMC7946428) SEP CRISPR knock-in at GluA2 N-terminus for surface visualisation; L9 (PMC8842155) HA at N-terminus of GluA2 detected by Western blot.

sources.claim: An amino-terminal hemagglutinin (HA) tag between the signal peptide and the amino-terminal domain served as the extracellular epitope.

literature_notes: All nine ledger lines were evaluated. L1, L2, L3, L4, L6, L7, and L9 all describe N-terminal tags on full-length, membrane-anchored GluA2 and converge on a single site (insert_after_residue=24). L8 describes an extracellular HA tag on GluA1 (a close ortholog) in Xenopus oocytes; it provides indirect corroboration of the same N-terminal position but does not add a new site and was not needed as the primary clip given the direct GluA2 evidence. L5 describes mNeonGreen fused to the cytoplasmic tail of GluA2(Q) and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports any insertion in the second extracellular domain (residues 646–812) or in any internal extracellular loop of GluA2; accordingly no such sites are proposed. Validation is surface_only rather than surface_and_function because none of the cited studies reports an electrophysiological or ligand-binding functional assay on the tagged GluA2 construct itself.

literature_other_positions.note: mNeonGreen appended to the cytoplasmic C-terminal tail of GluA2(Q) (PMC12152890); residue 883 (I) lies within the intracellular domain (834–883) and is not accessible for extracellular surface tagging.
